This week the UN voted to retire the Mercator projection, Israel dug in on a Lebanese ridge, and Russia opened a road bridge to North Korea across a river that never had one.

Five stories where the map itself is the news.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The UN General Assembly adopted a Togo-sponsored resolution to phase out Mercator in favour of Equal Earth.

Mercator (1569) was built for navigation: straight compass bearings, inflated poles. On it Greenland looks like Africa. Africa is ~14x bigger.

(Guardian, NYT)

2/ The AfD won Sunday's state election in Saxony-Anhalt — its best state result yet — but fell ~3 seats short of a majority and has no clear path to governing.

Merz's CDU slumped. A French minister called it a "grave moment" for Europe.

(BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera, NYT)

3/ Israeli air attacks on Kfar Reman in south Lebanon killed nine, with two medics killed in a separate drone strike.

Israel captured a strategic ridge last week and says it is cementing its foothold. Lebanon says the ceasefire is at risk.

(BBC, Al Jazeera, NYT)

4/ At least 60 killed on Yemen's west coast as Houthi forces push toward Bab al-Mandab, trying to take a port city and the high ground above the Red Sea entrance.

The strait is ~30km wide. It is the southern gate of the Suez route.

(Guardian, NYT, DW)

5/ Russia and North Korea opened the first road bridge across their shared border on the Tumen River.

The border is ~17km long. Until now the only fixed link was a rail bridge from 1959.

Single-sourced this cycle — reported by the Guardian.

The parallel: Saxony-Anhalt sits entirely inside the red here — the Soviet occupation zone of 1945, which became the GDR.

36 years after the border was erased, the AfD's vote is still highest almost exactly where the red was.

Full digest — including why every projection is a trade-off and what the old East German line still predicts — in this week's Lines & Legends. Free, every 3 days: https://buttondown.com/forummapping
